messages.subject: Bug in use of informative priors?
messages.subject_clean: Bug in use of informative priors?
messages.body_plain:
Dear Deal Users

I think I?ve found a bug in the way ?deal? handles informative priors. I?d
appreciate (1) comment on whether this is indeed a bug and (2), if it is
a bug, ideas on how to fix it.

First I?ve recreated the problem using the ?ksl? data set that comes with
the package. First I select three variables from this data set just to keep
things simple. For the same reason, I make each variable into a discrete
node. I use a different number of levels for each node, because I suspect
the problem is only apparent when some nodes have more than 2 levels.

rm(list=ls(all=TRUE))
library(deal)
data(ksl)
simple.df <- subset(ksl,select=2:4)
simple.df$Kol <- cut(simple.df$Kol, breaks=4, labels=c('1','2','3','4'))
simple.df$Hyp <- cut(simple.df$Hyp, breaks=2, labels=c('No','Yes'))
simple.df$logBMI <- cut(simple.df$logBMI, breaks=3, labels=c('Lo', 'Med',
'Hi'))

Second I just use the default which is an unspecified network and equi-probable
levels within each node. I set the imaginary database size to 1000, and after
learning the network, look at how the cases in the imaginary database have
been distributed among the levels of each node. As expected, the imaginary
database is spread out equally among the levels.

simple.nw <- network(simple.df)
simple.nw$nodes$Hyp$prob
simple.pr <- jointprior(simple.nw,1000)
simple.nw <- learn(simple.nw,simple.df,simple.pr)$nw
simple.nw$nodes$Hyp$prob
simple.nw$nodes$Hyp$condprior[[1]]$alpha
sum(simple.nw$nodes$Hyp$condprior[[1]]$alpha)

Third I repeat this but supply prior probabilities for each node. Oddly the
imaginary data base size now exceeds 1000, and the spread across the levels
of each node does not seem to reflect the priors I specified.

simple.nw <- network(simple.df)
simple.nw$nodes$Kol$prob <- c(0.1,0.1,0.1,0.7)
simple.nw$nodes$Hyp$prob <- c(0.1,0.9)
simple.nw$nodes$logBMI$prob <- c(0.25,0.25,0.50)
simple.nw$nodes$Hyp$prob
simple.pr <- jointprior(simple.nw,1000)
simple.nw <- learn(simple.nw,simple.df,simple.pr)$nw
simple.nw$nodes$Hyp$prob
simple.nw$nodes$Hyp$condprior[[1]]$alpha
sum(simple.nw$nodes$Hyp$condprior[[1]]$alpha)

Finally ? just to make absolutely sure ? I set the prior probabilities of
just one node. The imaginary data base size is now 1000 as expected but its
cases are distributed equally across the two levels of this node, which is
contrary to the prior probabilities I set for this node. 

simple.nw <- network(simple.df)
simple.nw$nodes$Hyp$prob <- c(0.1,0.9)
simple.nw$nodes$Hyp$prob
simple.pr <- jointprior(simple.nw,1000)
simple.nw <- learn(simple.nw,simple.df,simple.pr)$nw
simple.nw$nodes$Hyp$prob
simple.nw$nodes$Hyp$condprior[[1]]$alpha
sum(simple.nw$nodes$Hyp$condprior[[1]]$alpha)

So I really don?t think this is right. I have traced this odd behaviour to
?jointdisc?, an internal ?deal? function. But of course, there are no comments
with the code so it?s hard for me to know what each line in this function
is supposed to do. Therefore it?s hard to know what?s going wrong and how
to fix it.

Best wishes Jim

messages.body_plain:
Dear Deal Users

Further to my email of yesterday, I think in function jointdisc, the line:

ivek <- c(pidx, setdiff(jidx,pidx))

should read:

ivek <- c(idx, setdiff(jidx,idx)).

Well it seems to work for my example, but I hardly know what I am doing here
so who knows if solves a more general problem.

Best wishes Jim

messages.subject_clean: SV: Bug in use of informative priors?
messages.body_plain:
Dear Claus

Thanks for looking into this. I would have been amazed if my suggestion had
completely solved the problem. I?ve used it successfully on my example, where
I start with an unspecified network with five discrete nodes and these nodes
have 10, 3, 3, 2 and 2 levels respectively. And it seems to work on an example
I created using the ksl data with three discrete nodes, where one node has
a parent. So at best my suggestion might work for networks that consist entirely
of discrete nodes.

For networks with only discrete nodes, it?s easy to check whether everything
is working or not. After learning the parameters of the network, check the
?condprior? property of each node and make sure the cases sum to the imaginary
database size and are distributed as you asserted.

Best wishes Jim
